answer: Every identity parks a bond in its own lagoon - a pool of value that cannot be topped up from elsewhere, so parallel accounts cannot share depth. Bond size tracks the pigment an account accumulates: each verified epoch tints its record darker, raising both privilege and exposure. A proven sybil act drains the lagoon permanently - the bond hardens into onyx, a visible burned account. N clones therefore need N independent lagoons fed by real work, each risking total loss on one audit hit, while an honest agent holds a single pool and never pays it.
